# Unitree G1: Reproduction of ROCm for Predicted CBF

In this chapter, the predictive CBF control path in PAC-MAN is reproduced, and a full-body obstacle avoidance video is generated using the Unitree G1 model. The complete upstream training consists of mjlab, MuJoCo Warp, AMP［Adversarial Motion Prior］, and PPO［Proximal Policy Optimization］; in this tutorial, the safe control and ONNX［Open Neural Network Exchange Format］ policy that can be independently verified are first deployed on AMD PyTorch［AMD platform tensor computing framework］.

## Output of this chapter

- Fixed pitch trajectory and G1 full-body state replay;
- Statistics on minimum spacing, collisions, falls, and obstacle avoidance modes;
- Check of ONNX or PyTorch policy inputs and outputs;
- Commands for small-scale training, formal training, and fixed model evaluation;
- Static and conditional graph migration paths for MuJoCo Warp on AMD.

## 1. Download the source code and upstream assets

```bash
cd "$SRC_ROOT"
git clone https://github.com/lzyang2000/perceptive_cbf_rl.git
git clone https://github.com/Ethan-Chen-plus/radeon-physical-ai-evidence-suite.git

python -m pip install mujoco imageio imageio-ffmpeg onnxruntime
```

The upstream repository contains G1 MJCF, grids, action data, and `deploy/ckpts/dodge_link_cbf.onnx`.

## 2. CBF control path

The control obstacle function represents the margin with obstacles using a safety function `h(x)`. The safe set is `h(x) ≥ 0`. In discrete control, the safe layer selects the action `u` that is closest to the nominal action `u_nom`, while satisfying the next safety constraint:

```text
minimize    ||u - u_nom||²
subject to  h(x_next(u)) ≥ (1 - α) h(x)
```

`α` controls the contraction rate of safety margin. Link-CBF creates constraints based on the distance between robot links and balls, while Joint-CBF creates constraints in the joint space.

Predictive control is completed in sequence:

1. Estimate the horizontal trajectory based on the ball’s position and velocity;
2. Determine whether the ball is close, in the air, or within the perceived radius;
3. Select and store the avoidance direction perpendicular to the ball’s trajectory;
4. Project the nominal velocity into the time-constrained safe half-space;
5. Send the safe action to the G1 policy or the replay controller.

This tensor computation can be run in batches on ROCm［AMD Open Compute Platform］.

Output:

```text
g1_replay/

```

The playback results for 8 fixed seeds [random seeds] are kept at a safe distance of `8/8`, with a minimum distance of approximately 0.42 m.

## 5. ONNX Policy Inference

```bash
python - <<'PY'
import onnxruntime as ort

path = "src/perceptive_cbf_rl/deploy/ckpts/dodge_link_cbf.onnx"
session = ort.InferenceSession(path, providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"])
for value in session.get_inputs():
    print(value.name, value.shape, value.type)
for value in session.get_outputs():
    print(value.name, value.shape, value.type)
PY
```

If using the PyTorch [tensor computing framework] policy, the input consists of 960-dimensional features, and the output covers 29 joints. Check the stacking of input frames, normalization, joint order, and control frequency before execution.

## 6. Complete Training Configuration

Upstream training consists of mjlab, MuJoCo Warp, AMP［Adversarial Motion Prior］, and rsl_rl［Robot Reinforcement Learning Library］. Before training, synchronize dependencies and list registered environments:

```bash
cd "$SRC_ROOT/perceptive_cbf_rl"
uv sync
uv run python scripts/list_envs.py
```

The training matrix consists of three types of perceptual inputs and three safety constraints:

| Sensory Input | No Barrier Constraint | Link-CBF［Link Control Obstacle Function］ | Joint-CBF［Joint Control Obstacle Function］ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| State Oracle［True Value State］ | `state_none.sh` | `state_link.sh` | `state_joint.sh` |
| Fixed Camera［Fixed Camera］ | `vision_none.sh` | `vision_link.sh` | `vision_joint.sh` |
| Gimbal Camera［Gimbal Camera］ | `gimbal_none.sh` | `gimbal_link.sh` | `gimbal_joint.sh` |

Each script defaults to 8192 parallel environments and 25,000 iterations. The paper results fixly read the checkpoint of the 20,000th iteration. `vision_link.sh` is the configuration deployed on a real robot and exported as `deploy/ckpts/dodge_link_cbf.onnx`.

### 6.1 Small-scale Training Check

First, reduce the number of parallel environments and iterations, then verify asset loading, depth rendering, policy forward, backpropagation, and checkpoint saving:

```bash
cd "$SRC_ROOT/perceptive_cbf_rl"
NUM_ENVS=64 ./train_runs/vision_link.sh \
  --agent.max-iterations=10 \
  --video False
```

The training log should display the task `Unitree-G1-AMP-Dodge-Depth-Single-BallOnly-Flat`, the experiment name `vision_link_64`, and the continuously updated loss［loss value］. The output is located at:

```text
logs/rsl_rl/vision_link_64/{run}/
```

This step only verifies the training link, and is not used to report the obstacle avoidance success rate.

### 6.2 Formal Visual Policy Training

Run the paper configuration directly when VRAM is available:

```bash
cd "$SRC_ROOT/perceptive_cbf_rl"
NUM_ENVS=8192 ./train_runs/vision_link.sh
```

A single card with smaller resources can reduce the number of parallel environments. The script will append the number of environments to the experiment name to avoid overwriting the paper configuration:

```bash
NUM_ENVS=1024 ./train_runs/vision_link.sh
```

The visual policy reads the BallOnly masked depth [only retaining the mask depth map of the sphere], with a default camera elevation of 20 degrees, and uses a `(0,3,8,18)` four-frame offset. Training and deployment must maintain the same camera installation angle, joint order, control frequency, and depth preprocessing.

If you only want to verify the convergence of the security reward and PPO [proximal policy optimization] first, you can run the state policy that does not require depth rendering:

```bash
NUM_ENVS=8192 ./train_runs/state_link.sh
```

### 6.3 Fixed Checkpoint Evaluation

The upstream paper compares the checkpoint of the 20,000th iteration uniformly. First, determine the running directory, and then explicitly pass in the model file:

```bash
cd "$SRC_ROOT/perceptive_cbf_rl"
export DODGE_CKPT="$(find logs/rsl_rl/vision_link -name model_20000.pt -print -quit)"
test -f "$DODGE_CKPT"
echo "$DODGE_CKPT"

uv run python scripts/dodge_benchmark.py \
  --only vision_link \
  --ckpt "$DODGE_CKPT"
```

`DODGE_CKPT` will read the first matching model file. If there are multiple trainings for the same experiment, the old output should be deleted or the target file should be explicitly selected based on the training time. The deployment mode will also call the walking policy between two pitches to restore G1 to a standing position:

```bash
uv run python scripts/dodge_benchmark.py \
  --only vision_link \
  --walk-recover \
  --ckpt "$DODGE_CKPT"
```

Complete nine-group matrix evaluation runs directly:

```bash
uv run python scripts/dodge_benchmark.py
```

The evaluation should record the number of collisions, fall count, minimum safe distance, squat/left move/right move patterns, and single-step inference delay. Public videos can be selected from successful rounds, but the statistics table still uses the full denominator based on fixed checkpoint and fixed seed.

## 7. AMD Migration Route

Complete training cannot be achieved by simply replacing the PyTorch [tensor computing framework] installation package. It is necessary to migrate three levels: tensor computing, batch physical simulation, and computational graphs simultaneously.

| Level | Upstream Path | AMD Path | Verification Gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PPO/AMP | CUDA PyTorch | ROCm PyTorch | Forward, backward, optimizer updates |
| Batch Physics | MuJoCo Warp CUDA | AMD-Ecosystem MuJoCo Warp | State error and throughput under the same initial conditions |
| Conditional Graph | CUDA Graph conditional nodes | HIP Graph［AMD computational graph］ conditional nodes | Branch hit rate, physical equivalence, and acceleration ratio |
| Policy Deployment | ONNX Runtime | ONNX Runtime or ROCm PyTorch | Input shape, joint order, and latency |

First, download Warp and MuJoCo Warp maintained by AMD:

```bash
cd "$SRC_ROOT"
git clone https://github.com/AMD-Ecosystem/warp.git warp-amd
git clone https://github.com/AMD-Ecosystem/mujoco_warp.git mujoco-warp-amd
```

The AMD training environment should be isolated from the playback environment to prevent overlapping between different MuJoCo API versions. It is recommended to complete the process in the new environment step by step:

1. Verification of matrix calculations, backpropagation, and optimizer checks in ROCm PyTorch;
2. Asset loading for G1 MJCF and step-by-step execution in single-environment MuJoCo;
3. Static graph training verification for 64 parallel environments;
4. Validation of the equivalence between the `capture_while` condition solver and the `capture_if` dormancy island branch;
5. Comparison of throughput among three methods: step-by-step execution, static graph, and conditional graph;
6. Expanding parallel environments to 1024 or a scale that the devices can sustain reliably.

The acceleration results of the conditional graph must also meet the physical state error threshold. A mere increase in throughput, with the robot's position or contact state continuing to drift, cannot be considered equivalent training results.

## 8. Evaluation Metrics

| Metric | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| safe episode［Safe round］ | A round where the ball does not collide with the body and no fall occurs |
| minimum clearance［Minimum clearance］ | The closest distance between the ball trajectory and the body safety envelope |
| inference latency［Inference latency］ | The time taken for each CBF/policy call |
| moving joints［Number of moving joints］ | Whether the policy generates a full-body posture rather than translation replacement |
| dodge mode［Dodge mode］ | Crouching, left movement, right movement, or combined movements |
